question: What is the primary function of epithelial tissue?
solution: The correct answer is __**Protection**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Epithelial tissue** is one of the four basic types of tissues in the human body, alongside connective, muscular, and nervous tissues. • The primary function of epithelial tissue is **protection**. It serves as a barrier against physical, chemical, and biological harm, safeguarding the underlying structures of the body. • It forms the outer layer of the skin (epidermis) and lines internal organs, such as the gastrointestinal tract, respiratory tract, and blood vessels, providing a protective shield against external factors. • In addition to protection, epithelial tissue performs other functions such as **absorption, secretion, filtration, and sensory reception**, depending on its location and structure. • The specialized structure of epithelial tissue, including its tightly packed cells and minimal intercellular space, enhances its protective role by preventing the entry of pathogens and harmful substances.
